claims.text: R1008's profile keywords and bio centre on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for ICS protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling, kernel methods and lightweight online learning intended for constrained embedded environments; her stated fields include industrial cybersecurity, network traffic analysis, machine learning/statistical modelling and industrial control systems.
limitations: Profile fields are self-declared descriptions of expertise, not independently audited outputs.
The profile lists an interest in proprietary/undocumented protocols; it does not establish that BACnet is covered by her published work.

claims.text: R1008 co-authored a book chapter surveying statistical and machine-learning anomaly detection for ICS network traffic, covering univariate control charts, multivariate Gaussian models, kernel density estimators, one-class SVMs, Isolation Forest and autoencoders, with Modbus/DNP3/EtherNet/IP/PROFINET considerations and an explicit discussion of labelled-data scarcity and the false-alarm versus latency trade-off.
limitations: A survey chapter, not an experimental validation on the company's traffic.
Semantic support of the excerpt for specific method performance is unassessed.

claims.text: R1008 co-authored work on protocol-agnostic one-class detection using raw application-layer byte features (byte-frequency histograms, bigram entropy, MAD of byte values) with one-class SVM and Isolation Forest on mixed Modbus/DNP3/proprietary traffic, reporting AUROC 0.89 and 0.87 versus 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector, plus a decision framework on when parsed fields remain necessary.
limitations: Results are from her group's testbed, not from ArmaturaSec's field archives.
Higher accuracy came from protocol-aware parsing, so the protocol-agnostic route is a fallback rather than a like-for-like replacement.

claims.text: R1008's project work covers threshold calibration and incremental detector updates without labelled attack data, concept-drift-adapted incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder updates, cross-environment evaluation protocols, and a released Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark, with validation on a mirror-port feed from an operational substation network.
limitations: Project summaries are descriptive; specific calibration performance numbers are not given in the available evidence.
Validation was on an energy-distributor substation segment supplied by a partner, not on the company's client sites.

claims.text: R1008 also participated in a federated-learning project that aggregated site-level one-class classifier ensembles without exchanging raw traffic, piloted at two water utility control centres and two district heating substations, and published work on how OPC UA encryption modes reduce the feature set available to passive unsupervised detectors (6-feature one-class SVM detection rate 0.83 vs 0.91 with full 17 features).
limitations: The encryption-feature work concerns OPC UA, not Modbus TCP or BACnet/IP.
Federated pilot sites were utilities in a border region, not ArmaturaSec customers.

claims.text: R1008's group runs an ICS testbed with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators and long-term packet-capture infrastructure, and has acted as monitoring data partner with an energy distributor and a water utility plus paid consulting on anomaly-detection requirements for a SCADA upgrade.
limitations: Testbed availability is stated as conditional on a data-sharing agreement.
Industry experience is described at summary level without named references for verification.

claims.text: R1008's open-to list and notes indicate an explicit willingness to take on the challenge's shape of work: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring, contract research on anomaly-detection deployment, consulting on detector calibration and evaluation methodology, and deployment on real rather than purely synthetic infrastructure — matching the company's need for a site-specific unsupervised baseline plus explainable alerting.
limitations: Open-to statements are declared availability, not a confirmed commitment or capacity for this engagement.
She states a preference for deployment on real infrastructure, which constrains purely offline or simulated work.

claims.text: Bounded pilot (about 6 months, 1–2 company engineers part-time plus one of her researchers): use only consenting clients' unlabelled captures to fit per-site one-class baselines (starting with control charts / multivariate Gaussian or one-class SVM variants she has surveyed), calibrate alert thresholds without attack labels, and report a precision-oriented false-alarm budget per site alongside drift response after planned process changes.
limitations: No confirmed attack data exists, so true detection rate cannot be measured; the pilot must therefore be scored on false-alarm rate, stability and expert triage, not recall.
Threshold calibration without labels can only give approximate guarantees about missed detections.

claims.text: Validation should use her testbed and labelled Modbus/TCP benchmark for pipeline sanity checks and method comparison only, while field validation uses the company's normal-traffic archives on a site-by-site holdout protocol (fit on early capture windows, evaluate on later windows), and explainability is delivered as per-feature baseline-deviation descriptions a plant manager can read.
limitations: Benchmark attack scenarios were injected on a laboratory testbed, so benchmark results may not transfer to field traffic.
Explainability output format is a proposal; no evidence in the record establishes plant-manager usability.

claims.text: Remaining open technical questions: whether BACnet/IP behaviour is covered by her published experience (the evidence stresses Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET and OPC UA), whether encrypted or proprietary segments reduce available features as in the OPC UA study, and how detector thresholds should be recalibrated when firmware or process changes cause drift.
limitations: This is an inference from absence of BACnet coverage in the retrieved records, not proof that she has no BACnet experience.
The candidate pool is a truncated lexical retrieval set with unassessed semantic support and uncalibrated relevance.

summary.text: R1008 is a strong technical match: her declared and published work is unsupervised/one-class anomaly detection and statistical baseline modelling for ICS protocol traffic, including calibration without labelled attacks and incremental drift updates, which maps directly onto ArmaturaSec's need to flag Modbus/BACnet behaviour that departs from a per-site normal baseline. She also states willingness to work on real deployments and to consult on detector calibration and evaluation methodology.

technicalRationale.text: Her evidence base covers exactly the design space the company needs: statistical and ML anomaly detectors with embedded-deployment suitability, calibration procedures without labels, incremental updates for concept drift, multi-protocol score aggregation, and reduced-feature detection when encryption hides payload detail. Protocol-agnostic byte features offer a possible route for BACnet or proprietary traffic where parsing is weak.

cooperationScope.text: Proposed scope: contract research or joint project on per-site unsupervised baselining and threshold calibration for ProtoSense, plus consulting on evaluation methodology and deployment architecture; possible student internship or industrial PhD route via her open-to list.

validation.text: Validation plan: lab sanity checks and method comparison on her labelled Modbus/TCP benchmark and testbed, then field evaluation on consenting clients' unlabelled archives using temporal holdout windows per site, scored on false-alarm rate, alert stability, drift response and engineer triage agreement; explainability checked against plain-language plant-manager review.

constraints.text: Her notes state a preference for deployment on real infrastructure over purely synthetic experiments, and testbed access is conditional on a data-sharing agreement; she also flags proprietary/undocumented protocols as an interest area. Labelling constraints on the company side (zero confirmed attacks) limit what detection-rate claims can be made.

findings.explanation: R0305's notes state explicitly that she 'prefers partnerships where the company can share even a small number of labelled anomaly examples, as her methods rely on partial supervision' and that she 'is not interested in purely unsupervised or image-based projects'. Her bio and keywords describe supervised anomaly detection and imbalanced classification (E023, E081). C001-CH1 states there are zero labelled malicious examples and rejects supervised classifiers, so her own stated restriction and method profile exclude the core ask. Any pairing must be re-justified or dropped.
findings.recheckQuestion: Given the challenge's explicit zero-label constraint and R0305's stated non-interest in purely unsupervised work, is there any sub-task (e.g., threshold calibration on operator-labelled drift episodes) that does not require attack labels, and would R0305 accept it?

findings.explanation: R0548's profile, keywords and all ten listed publications concern computer vision: image-based surface/defect inspection, video anomaly detection, visual few-shot learning, image quantisation and edge-cloud visual inference (E098, E015, E159, E165, E043). No registered evidence shows any work on network traffic, Modbus, BACnet, packet captures or protocol features. The lexical match on 'anomaly detection', 'few-shot' and 'edge inference' does not establish protocol-traffic suitability. His edge-quantisation expertise is transferable only in principle.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0548 have any unregistered or unpublished network-traffic anomaly detection work that would let him contribute beyond generic edge-model compression?

findings.explanation: R0039's structured profile (open_to, notes, industry_experience, keywords) presents a recommender-systems/IR researcher serving e-commerce and digital media partners (E064, E133, E114); his bio field is empty. Seven of the listed publications in the bundle are recommender/ANN/OOD-text work (E062, E006, E121, E102). The single ICS item, SYN-PUB-00492 on incremental Gaussian mixtures for Modbus/TCP traffic (E021, E048), is only a co-authored contribution whose abstract reports comparison against a static model retrained every 24 hours on a '180-day Modbus/TCP capture'; the abstract does not state that the capture was unlabelled and mentions a 'supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement'. Attaching his recommender-systems open_to/industry profile to an OT-security engagement is one-sided and unsupported.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which parts of SYN-PUB-00492 (E048) did R0039 personally contribute, and was the training baseline label-free for the 180-day Modbus capture?

findings.explanation: R0416's own note frames her interest as companies needing 'structured behavioural models for testing, monitoring, or certification purposes' and says she 'prefers project engagements where there is a defined research question rather than pure development work' (E163), consistent with her open_to list (E058). Her single OT-adjacent pilot lasted 2018-2020 with a small embedded systems company (E082). Her anomaly-detection evidence rests on automaton/HMM baselines over message-type sequences, with self-reported weakness on field mutation (E036), testbed SCADA sessions with injected anomalies, and IoT metadata inference (E173). The ICS-relevant detector is a 'secondary objective' of SYN-PRJ-1055 (E110) and FORMIOT targets smart-building IoT devices (E177). No registered evidence covers Modbus/BACnet field-level features, drift-baseline learning on multi-year archives, or product-grade deployment.
findings.recheckQuestion: Has the automaton-based detector from SYN-PRJ-1055 been evaluated on Modbus/TCP or BACnet captures, and would R0416 accept a product-oriented delivery role that she says she prefers to avoid?

findings.explanation: R0071's notes state limited capacity for new long-term commitments 'before mid-2025' while co-supervising two PhD students (E083); this capacity window is stale relative to the run and may already be expired, but it has not been updated by registered evidence. Her method portfolio is label-hungry where it is strongest: constrained OC-SVM needs partial anomaly labels (E053), self-training starts from 2% labelled data (E026/E054), and supervised drift ensembles are used in DRIFTGUARD (E140). Her explicit preference for 'real labelled or partially labelled sensor datasets' (E083) runs against the challenge's fully unlabelled OT network setting. She has no registered Modbus/BACnet or packet-capture research.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is R0071's stated limited capacity still in force after mid-2025, and does her OC-SVM work have a label-free configuration usable with zero attack examples?

findings.explanation: R0738's open_to list is restricted to companies operating PV parks, wind farms or district heating networks (E130), and his notes state coordination capacity is limited until 2027 with preference for partners supplying labelled fault telemetry (E075). All registered content concerns SCADA sensor telemetry for energy assets: sensor-drift autoencoders on PV monitoring (E094), isolation forest on district-heating substation telemetry (E065), and time-series foundation model benchmarking on energy SCADA (E107). His keywords contain no network-security or protocol terms (E175). The baseline/drift framing is conceptually close, but nothing in the bundle addresses packet-level Modbus/BACnet traffic or malicious-network-behaviour semantics.
findings.recheckQuestion: Would R0738 accept an OT network-traffic partner that is not a PV/wind/heating operator, and does he have any network-traffic (as opposed to telemetry) anomaly detection evidence?

findings.explanation: R1008 has the strongest topical fit (unsupervised/one-class ICS protocol anomaly detection, Modbus, offline/incremental detectors, deployment-oriented consulting; E032, E149, E004). However, several of her registered contributions are built around labelled attack data: the 21-day/6-day labelled Modbus/TCP benchmark with binary normal/attack flags (E093, E109, E135) and the multi-protocol score aggregation study whose best strategy 'required labelled data for weight estimation' and was trained on a '5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination' (E105). The challenge demands a method with no attack examples at all, so claims must be scoped to her label-free work (one-class SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, control charts in E032) rather than to the labelled-benchmark infrastructure. Her abstraction-level coverage of BACnet is also absent (see F08).
findings.recheckQuestion: Which of R1008's published detectors were trained and thresholded without any labelled attack data, and which BACnet evidence exists outside the registered bundle?

findings.explanation: The challenge is jointly about Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP (the ProtoSense module parses both). In the complete registered evidence for all eight candidates, no evidence record mentions BACnet: Modbus appears in R1008 (E063, E093), R1015 (E060, E090), R0039 (E048); the remaining candidates cover DNP3, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET or non-network data. Any plan implying validated BACnet anomaly detection capability is unsupported by the registered evidence and must be treated as an open work item rather than a demonstrated capability.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which candidate can point to registered evidence of BACnet/IP behaviour modelling or detection, and if none, how will BACnet parity be achieved within the collaboration?

findings.explanation: R1015's most on-point publication trains an autoencoder on benign-only Modbus traffic, but evaluation uses a dataset 'generated from a real-world PLC testbed' with injected attack scenarios and reports >94% detection at <2% false positives on that synthetic set (E060). No registered evidence covers evaluation on unlabelled operational traffic, multi-year site baselines, or deployment hardening. His other publications concern federated IoT intrusion detection (E010), smart-building STRIDE threat modelling (E148) and framework gap analysis (E050), none of which demonstrate BACnet traffic detection or explainable flagging. His industry_experience field is empty and his notes are empty, so his collaboration constraints are thinly documented; open_to is limited to 'industrial PhD supervision' and 'joint projects' (E150).
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R1015 have results on unlabelled operational traffic beyond the synthetic testbed dataset, and what availability/commitment terms underpin 'joint projects'?

findings.explanation: The challenge requires a method explainable to a plant manager in plain language. The registered abstracts describe autoencoders, one-class SVMs, Isolation Forest, incremental Gaussian mixtures, ensemble stacking and automaton models, and report detection, F1, AUROC and latency metrics, but none reports operator-facing explanation output, interpretability evaluation with non-specialists, or plain-language flag rationale. E032 notes kernel methods and autoencoders among candidate algorithms for embedded deployment without explaining how their alarms would be justified to an operator; R0416's note references certification/monitoring models (E163) and R0305 relies on partial supervision (E104), neither of which supplies operator explainability evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which candidate has registered or plannable evidence of operator-evaluated explanation of individual flags, rather than only aggregate detection metrics?

findings.explanation: C4 attributes to R1008, via project participation in SYN-PRJ-0511 (E169, E113), the 'concept-drift-adapted incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder updates' and a 'Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark'. E169 does say ICAROS developed incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder update algorithms with threshold calibration without labelled attack data, so that part is supported at project level; but the concrete evidence for an incremental Gaussian mixture detector on 180-day Modbus/TCP traffic with a supervised operator-acknowledgement reset (E048, SYN-PUB-00492 / E018) is a publication whose author list (E132 record context) shows R1008 as fourth author alongside R0039 and others, and C4 does not cite E048/E018 for the technical content while the summary and rationale lean on the drift-adapted detector as her contribution. More importantly, C4 ties the released labelled Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark to her calibration work even though the challenge explicitly has no labelled attack data; presenting a labelled benchmark as part of her label-free toolkit blurs the key distinction. Fix C4 to cite E048 for the iGMM content, state her fourth-author role, and separate the labelled benchmark (sanity-check use only, as C9 already does) from the label-free calibration line.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can C4 be rewritten so the incremental Gaussian-mixture/drift evidence cites E048 (with R1008's co-author position shown) and the labelled benchmark is explicitly confined to the C9 sanity-check role rather than presented as part of the zero-label calibration capability?

findings.explanation: C7 concludes that her open_to list and notes 'match the company's need for a site-specific unsupervised baseline plus explainable alerting'. E004 and E149 support contract research on anomaly-detection deployment, consulting on detector calibration/evaluation methodology, real-infrastructure deployment, and testbed under a data-sharing agreement — but nothing in E004, E149 or E126 mentions explainability, plain-language alert rationale, BACnet/IP, multi-terabyte archives, on-device (DIN-rail/security-processor) inference under latency constraints, or drift-baseline learning on multi-year site archives. The C7 text also claims she will take on 'explainable alerting', which no cited evidence supports; C9's limitations concede explainability is only a proposal and Counter F10 was right that no registered evidence covers operator-facing explanations. C7 must be narrowed to what E004/E149 actually state (contract research/joint project on anomaly detection deployment, calibration and evaluation consulting, real-infrastructure preference, testbed under DSA), and any explainability plan must be labeled as an unvalidated new work item with the engineer resource.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which exact words in E004/E149 support deployment-oriented calibration and evaluation work (not explainability or BACnet), and can C7 be restricted to those, with explainability moved to a plainly-labeled work item in constraints/unknowns?

findings.explanation: The challenge's ProtoSense targets Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP jointly. R1008's registered evidence covers Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET (E032), a proprietary protocol (E063), OPC UA (E153) and ICS project work (E169); no record mentions BACnet. C10 honestly lists BACnet as an open question and the summary correctly describes the project as Modbus/BACnet but the cooperation mechanism rests on her evidence for Modbus-family protocols. Because zero-label site-specific baselining for BACnet is a core half of the ask, the proposal needs an explicit, source-grounded path for BACnet (e.g., the protocol-agnostic byte-feature route in E063 applied to BACnet PDUs, or her stated interest in proprietary/undocumented protocols in E149) rather than only an unknown. As drafted the plan's core contribution to the selected challenge is only half-evidenced.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the proposal cite a registered mechanism by which R1008's label-free methods (e.g., E063 protocol-agnostic byte features, E032 embedded-suitable methods) would be applied to BACnet/IP, and is that stated as the concrete BACnet work item within the bounded six-month pilot?

findings.explanation: C8 correctly limits the pilot to label-free fitting, but its reference to method families 'she has surveyed' (E032) and the field validation protocol drawn from E169 does not cite the registered evidence that the training itself required labels in several of her works (E105 learned linear combination needed labelled weights; the benchmark in E093 is fully labelled). C8's limitation section admits no attack data exists, but it would be clearer to cite E169's threshold-calibration-without-labels explicitly as the basis and to state that E105's aggregation is out of scope. C9 does handle the labelled benchmark as sanity-check only, which is appropriate.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can C8 cite E169 (threshold calibration without labelled attack data) as the explicit basis and state that label-dependent components such as E105's learned aggregation are excluded from the field phase?

findings.explanation: E149 conditions testbed capacity on a data-sharing agreement, and E004 says testbed/capture access is offered for collaborative experiments. The draft's constraints mention the data-sharing agreement and the multi-terabyte archive sharing question, which is good. However, the cooperationScope mentions 'possible student internship or industrial PhD route' from E004 without noting she is at full professor level with existing commitments (no capacity statement appears in her notes, unlike R0071/R0738), and C8's '1–2 company engineers part-time plus one of her researchers' is not grounded in any registered statement about her staffing. That is a plan assumption, not a supported commitment; it should be flagged as an assumption to confirm, not presented as part of the match.
findings.recheckQuestion: Should the pilot staffing and internship/PhD framing be marked as unconfirmed assumptions rather than evidence-based aspects of the collaboration scope, given E004/E149 contain no capacity or staffing commitments?

findings.explanation: C9 proposes per-feature baseline-deviation descriptions as the plant-manager explanation and honestly notes no evidence supports usability. That is acceptable as a bounded proposal, but the validation section says explainability will be 'checked against plain-language plant-manager review' without stating who evaluates, against which criterion, or that this is a novel evaluation not drawn from registered evidence. Given the challenge's explicit plain-language requirement, add a concrete evaluation criterion in the validation text (reviewer set, task, pass criterion) so the deliverable is testable rather than aspirational.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can the validation section specify the concrete plant-manager explanation test (who reviews, what task, what pass criterion) so the explainability deliverable is falsifiable within the six-month pilot?

E169 does support threshold calibration 'without labelled attack data' and incremental GMM/autoencoder update algorithms, but only at project-summary level with no configuration detail, and the same project released a labelled Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark.
